content: 1. Peginterferon alfa-2a can increase the levels or effects of ondansetron by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Pentamidine and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. These drugs should be avoided or alternative medications should be used, especially in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when co-administering medications that prolong the QT interval, in the presence of electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure (CHF), or bradyarrhythmias. 3. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Pentobarbital also decreases ondansetron levels via CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Perphenazine and ondansetron both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended in patients with congenital long QT syndrome or when co-administering QT-prolonging medications. 6.
